The most recent observation shows VIX at 31.05, up sharply from 26.78 in the prior period—a 4-point jump representing the largest single move in this dataset. The 4-week momentum measure (vix_change_4w) confirms sustained upward pressure at 11.19 points, more than double the prior reading of 7.69. The vol risk premium has also widened to 0.23, matching the elevated level seen at the peak of the prior spike.

This is unambiguous regime reversal. The VIX has breached and held above the 30 level—territory that appears only once elsewhere in this data and signals genuine tail risk repricing. The gap between implied volatility and realized volatility (the premium) has widened proportionally, indicating this is not merely statistical but reflects genuine demand for downside protection. The momentum remains decisively upward, with the most recent 4-week change the strongest in the series.

My previous falsifier condition—VIX sustained above 21 with premium above 0.12—has not merely been met but decisively exceeded. The regime has shifted to elevated equity volatility with structural support from both the level and the premium. The evidence no longer supports an easing call.

For the one-month horizon ahead, the momentum and absolute level suggest volatility is likely to remain elevated. A mean-reversion to pre-spike levels would require substantial new stabilizing information. The current regime appears entrenched.
